title: Rate limiting for the Orders API
subtitle: feature/rate-limit → main

scenes.narration: This merge request protects the orders endpoint from bursts of traffic, prices orders from the pricing service, and emits an event for every new order. It adds no tests, so the review rests on reading the code.
scenes.summary: Add Redis-backed rate limiting to POST /orders and publish order.created events.
bullets: A Redis outage now fails every order request, because the limiter has no fallback
publish runs after the insert, so a queue outage returns an error for an order that was saved
No tests cover the limiter, the pricing lookup, or the new event

scenes.narration: Requests now pass through a rate limiter backed by Redis before reaching the orders service, which writes to the database and then publishes to the event queue.

scenes.title: POST /orders
scenes.narration: Here is the new call order. The API asks Redis to count the request before the orders service runs. After the insert, the API publishes the event without waiting for anyone to consume it.

scenes.title: POST /orders
scenes.narration: Follow one request. The limiter counts it, the service prices the items and saves the order, and the API publishes a compact event before responding.

scenes.title: orders
scenes.narration: The orders table gains a status column, starting as pending. Totals are now computed from the pricing service, and each order still belongs to one user with many line items.

The limiter buckets each IP into a one-minute window, increments a Redis counter, and sets the expiry only on the first hit. Past twenty requests it answers 429 with a Retry-After header. Otherwise the request moves on.
scenes.calloutText: Expiry is set once per window, so the key cleans itself up.

flow.label: Count this request in the IP's one-minute window
On the first hit, expire the key with the window
Over the limit? Refuse the request
flow.outcome: Past twenty: too many requests, with Retry-After

flow.label: Under the limit, pass the request on

scenes.narration: The server mounts the limiter on the orders route and publishes an event after the order is saved.
scenes.calloutText: publish runs after the insert, so a queue outage fails the request.

scenes.narration: Order totals used a hard-coded price of ten. They now look up each SKU in parallel, and empty orders are rejected up front.
scenes.calloutText: Pricing lookups run in parallel with Promise.all.

scenes.title: Test coverage
scenes.subject: rateLimit, createOrder and the orders route
scenes.narration: This change adds no tests. Nothing checks that the twenty first request in a minute gets too many requests, what happens when Redis or the queue is down, or that empty orders are rejected.
gaps: The twenty first request in a minute from one IP gets 429 with a Retry-After header
When Redis is down the limiter throws, so every order request fails
When the queue is down after the insert, the client gets an error for an order that was saved
Empty orders are rejected and totals use prices from the pricing service
